key_highlights: Fed raises rates for first time since 2023 under hawkish Chair Warsh, defying Trump; 10-year Treasury yield hits 5%, highest since 2007
Dow falls 400 points as markets reprice higher-for-longer rate expectations; Warsh gains credibility boost
Oil stays above $100/bbl; Asia diesel refining margins hit record $87/bbl; China yuan crude futures at record high
Gold holds ~$4,300 range; silver rises pre-Fed; both swing lower post-hike as dollar strengthens
AI sector mixed: OpenAI acquires Glass Imaging ($300M), Micron launches new memory module, but Google DeepMind researchers warn of AI apocalypse; Cruz/Hawley push antitrust exemptions for AI
Foreign holdings of US Treasuries fell to 9-month low in July; dollar lifts on hawkish Fed
Robinhood expands into Canada with tokenized stocks; SpaceX Starship orbital launch Sept 22; Musk hints at SpaceX-Tesla merger
Clarity Act cloture vote fails, pressuring crypto (Coinbase -6%, Strategy -5%); CoinEx to shut down
Carney positions Canada as 'safe harbour' for global finance at Toronto Summit
Airlines (United, American) warn fuel cost surge may force capacity cuts

sectors.implications: Energy inflation feeds into broader CPI; airline margins under pressure; biofuel policy creates trade friction; refining sector benefits

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish-to-neutral. Fed hike and 5% 10-year yield create headwinds for equities. Dow -400 pts signals risk-off. Oil >$100 and diesel records sustain inflation pressure. Crypto weak on Clarity Act failure. Gold/silver volatile around Fed. Expect 1-2% equity drawdowns in coming weeks as rate repricing continues.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive. AI capex cycle and space economy maturation provide structural growth. Canadian financial sector offers diversification. Energy sector benefits from commodity strength. However, sustained high rates and trade war risks cap multiples. 6-12 month path depends on whether Fed stabilizes and oil normalizes below $90.
key_catalysts: Fed Warsh follow-through on rate path (next FOMC)
